svg.title: AI-native bug path: diagnose and approve scope before code changes
svg.desc: A human or AI agent creates a Jira Bug, triggering investigation in approved repositories, supported by catalog and code-graph candidates when available. Human acceptance of diagnosis and scope leads to bounded implementation and verification, then a draft GitHub pull request and authorized merge. The Bug owner identifies who verifies resolution afterward. When configured, an authorized agent can post concise Bug and investigation updates with links to a designated Teams channel. A branch from the human gate shows needs-information, blocked, no-action, or non-code outcomes without a pull request. New information or a changed repository baseline prompts revalidation; material changes require renewed human acceptance, and triage restarts when the diagnosis may no longer hold.
svg.text: Bug path: diagnose and approve scope before code changes
The cause and affected repository may be unknown at intake.

g.text: Human or AI agent records behavior, impact, and evidence.
Creating the Jira Bug triggers triage.
Catalog and graph suggest candidates when available.
Agent inspects only approved sources; reports likely cause,
alternatives, evidence, proposed fix and regression checks.
Person confirms the diagnosis, affected repos and scope.
Complex or cross-repo work needs a fuller plan and order.
Agent changes only accepted scope and adds a regression check.
Local review and checks; material changes need revalidation.
Implementation agent opens linked draft PR(s).
CI and review follow; authorized merge; owner checks outcome.
route or close without a PR.

svg.text: Teams updates are notifications; Jira links decisions and evidence; the agent runtime retains the detailed run.
